transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been going on that made you decide to come see me?

I... well, it's about my house. Everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork, or missed payments. But... I know what's actually going on. 

The bank, the loan servicer... even some of the people at my job. They've been quietly working together to push me out. I've been seeing it happen for almost two years now. And... no amount of papers they try to show me is going to change what I know I've been seeing.
When you look back at the evidence you've gathered about the bank and your job working together, do you ever have any doubt that this is actually happening, or are you completely certain about it?

I... no. I don't have any doubt. 

Like I just said, it doesn't matter what papers they try to show me. I know what I've been seeing for the last two years. The bank, my work... I know they're doing it. 

So, yes. I'm certain. I wouldn't be saying it if I wasn't.

When you say you've been 'seeing' what the bank and your job are doing together, do you mean you've actually heard voices or seen things that others around you don't seem to notice? Or are you basing this on things you've observed and put together in your own mind?

I... no. I don't hear voices. Or see things that aren't there. 

It's just... things I've noticed. How people act. What happens. I just put it together. That's all.
You mentioned this has been going on for almost two years. When did you first start noticing these things about the bank and your job working together? Can you remember when it started?

It's been... about a year and nine months, I guess. 

That's when the... the foreclosure notices started showing up in the mail. And the phone calls from the bank. It just kind of took over everything at home. 

That's when I started noticing it.

You mentioned the bank and your job are working together against you. Can you walk me through exactly how you think they're communicating with each other, or what specific steps you believe they're taking together? I want to understand the full picture of how you think this conspiracy is operating.

I... I don't know exactly how they talk to each other. It's not like they copy me on the emails or anything. 

I just... I see what happens. I'm not in the room with them when they plan it, so I don't know the specific steps. I just see how things get changed around at the store, and then the bank does what it does. 

I don't know exactly how they do it. I just know that they are.
Besides the bank and your job working together, do you believe other people or organizations are also involved in this against you, or is it mainly just these two?

Well... the loan servicer is part of it, too. But I think that's it. 

Everyone just keeps acting like this whole foreclosure is... I don't know, just paperwork. Like it's just about missed payments. But I know the bank, the loan servicer, and the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. 

They can show me all the papers they want. It doesn't change what I've been seeing.

How much has this belief about the bank, loan servicer, and your job working together affected your daily life? Has it changed how you're able to work, take care of yourself, or interact with people around you?

I mean... I still do my job. I go in, I handle the schedules, deal with customers, make sure my team is doing what they need to do. I take care of myself fine. 

It's just... when the mail comes. Or the phone rings and it's the bank. Or when they hand me certain paperwork at the store. That's when it's hard. But if it's not about the house... I just do what I'm supposed to do.

Apart from what's happening with the bank, loan servicer, and your job, do you have concerns that other people or groups in your life might also be working against you in some way, or is it really just these three that you're worried about?
No. Just them. I haven't noticed anyone else.

When you think about what the bank, loan servicer, and your job are doing to push you out of your house—is this something that you believe could actually happen in the real world, even if it seems unlikely? Or does it seem like something that would be impossible or go against the laws of nature?

I don't really know what you mean by laws of nature. It's not... magic. 

It's just people making deals behind closed doors. Businesses talk to each other all the time. It happens in the real world every day. So... yes. It's possible. Because it's exactly what they're doing.

Before all of this started with the bank and your job, have you ever had concerns in the past that other people or groups were working against you in different situations—maybe at previous jobs, in relationships, or in other parts of your life? Or is this the first time you've felt like people were conspiring against you?
No. This is the first time. I've never had a reason to think anything like this before. Like I said, it's just them.

You've told me about the bank, loan servicer, and your job working together. But thinking more broadly about your life right now—do you have any other strong beliefs about things happening to you or around you that seem unusual or that other people don't seem to notice or agree with? Anything else that feels significant to you?
No. Just what I already told you. I don't... there's nothing else going on. Just the situation with my house.

If someone you trusted completely—like a family member or close friend—told you that they had looked into this situation carefully and believed the bank, loan servicer, and your job were NOT actually working together, would that make you question your own belief at all, or would you still be certain they were working together?

I don't think they could convince me otherwise. I mean, I'm here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just... paperwork. Like it's just missed payments. But I know they've been quietly working together to push me out of my house. 

If someone showed me different papers... it wouldn't matter. No amount of papers they show me changes what I've been seeing for almost two years. So... no. I'd still be certain.
